ANYmal gains secure door access for industrial inspection

ANYbotics, dormakaba and LEGIC tested automated access at Whitegate power station, combining robot credentials with existing site permissions.

The Robot Report ↗24 September 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2Videos 1

Removing a route barrier

ANYbotics, dormakaba and LEGIC are enabling ANYmal to pass through industrial doors, including access-controlled areas. The aim is to extend inspection routes without staff opening doors, while retaining the site’s safety barriers.

Two access mechanisms

At unlocked doors, radar triggers a dormakaba ED 100 or ED 250 operator. For locked doors, LEGIC digital credentials let the exos access system check authorization before unlocking. Operators can restrict permissions by zone, time window and task.

Tested in an operating power station

The companies report several weeks of testing at GE Vernova’s Whitegate power station in County Cork, Ireland. ANYmal requested access, crossed controlled doors and completed inspection routes without manual intervention in those steps, with timestamped records for auditing.

Existing security still matters

The system does not replace measures against people following an authorized user through a door. Existing site protections remain necessary. The access-control add-on is planned for later in 2026 for installed systems and future ANYmal hardware.
